prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_E:
The Liberal Democrats’ 2024 manifesto offers a Fair Deal to replace an out‑of‑touch Conservative government, fix broken systems, and restore a fair, free and open society. It centres on green prosperity, strong public services, internationalism, civil liberties and genuine power for communities.

- Economy and jobs: Drive a green recovery with large-scale investment in renewables, home insulation and skills; boost apprenticeships and create Lifelong Skills Grants; overhaul parental leave to increase choice; back entrepreneurs and small firms, replacing business rates with a fairer Commercial Landowner Levy; manage public finances responsibly; cut barriers to trade by fixing relations with Europe; fund priorities by reversing Conservatives’ tax cuts for big banks, imposing a proper windfall tax on oil and gas, reforming capital gains and taxing FTSE share buybacks.

- NHS and care: A new right to see a GP within seven days (24 hours if urgent), backed by 8,000 more GPs; guaranteed urgent NHS dentistry; mental health hubs for young people and a trained professional in every school; a cancer treatment guarantee within 62 days; invest in prevention and diagnostics; fix social care with free personal care, a workforce plan, a Royal College of Care Workers and a higher “Carer’s Minimum Wage,” plus paid carer’s leave and regular respite.

- Climate, energy and nature: Net zero by 2045; 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030; a 10‑year home energy upgrade with free insulation and heat pumps for low‑income households; a rooftop solar revolution; decouple electricity from gas prices; ban fracking and new coal; expand storage and interconnectors; empower community energy. End the sewage scandal by reforming water companies as public benefit companies, creating a tough new regulator and binding anti‑dumping targets; double nature by 2050; Clean Air Act; plant 60 million trees a year.

- Housing and communities: Build 380,000 homes a year, including 150,000 social homes, through garden cities and community‑led development; zero‑carbon new homes; “Rent to Own” for social housing; end rough sleeping and scrap the Vagrancy Act; ban no‑fault evictions, make three‑year tenancies the default; abolish leasehold and cap ground rents; give councils powers over second homes and short‑term lets; deliver gigabit broadband everywhere; decentralise power and funding.

- Education and families: Increase per‑pupil funding above inflation; a Tutoring Guarantee for disadvantaged pupils; mental health support in every school; boost early years with more free hours and a higher Early Years Pupil Premium; restore maintenance grants; £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants for adults; expand free school meals to all children in poverty; double Statutory Maternity and Shared Parental Pay and add a use‑it‑or‑lose‑it month for fathers; return to Erasmus+.

- Transport: Make EVs affordable (more chargers, restore plug‑in grant, 2030 zero‑emission sales rule); freeze rail fares and simplify ticketing; electrify rail, deliver Northern Powerhouse Rail; empower councils to restore bus routes; invest in walking and cycling; fix local roads and potholes.

- Rights, policing and justice: Restore community policing with a guarantee that all burglaries are attended; tackle court backlogs; end disproportionate Stop and Search; fund VAWG support and trauma‑informed justice; defend the Human Rights Act; ban conversion therapy; make misogyny a hate crime; scrap anti‑protest laws; strengthen disability rights and flexible working.

- Immigration and asylum: End the Hostile Environment; scrap the Illegal Migration Act and the Rwanda scheme; create safe and legal routes; clear the asylum backlog with a three‑month decision standard and allow work after three months; introduce flexible, merit‑based work visas; protect EU citizens’ rights.

- Political reform: Proportional representation for Westminster and English councils; votes at 16; cap political donations; put the Ministerial Code into law; reform the Lords; a written federal constitution and stronger devolution.

- Defence and international: Reverse Army cuts and move towards spending 2.5% of GDP on defence; maintain NATO commitment and the nuclear deterrent; tighten arms exports; support Ukraine and seize frozen Russian assets; restore 0.7% aid; rebuild Europe ties through a step‑by‑step roadmap towards the Single Market; back an immediate ceasefire and a two‑state solution in Israel‑Palestine; stand up to authoritarian regimes.

TEXT_A:
The Green Party’s manifesto offers a hopeful, science-led plan to tackle the intertwined crises of living costs, inequality and climate breakdown, replacing failed market dogma with fairness, public investment and democratic control.

Core promise
- A rapid, just transition to a zero‑carbon, nature‑positive economy that delivers warmer homes, better public services, secure jobs and lower bills—funded by fair taxation on extreme wealth and pollution, and by borrowing to invest.

Health and care
- Rebuild a fully public NHS, end privatisation and pay staff fairly; cut waits via investment in hospitals, primary care, dentistry and mental health; expand diagnostics; a National Cancer Plan.
- Free personal care for older and disabled people; a funded workforce plan and fair pay; £20bn a year for social care.
- Dignity and rights for disabled people, children in care and unpaid carers.

Homes
- 150,000 new social homes a year; end Right to Buy; rent controls; end no‑fault evictions.
- Passivhaus‑level standards for new builds; a ten‑year, council‑led retrofit with grants and property‑linked finance to slash bills and emissions.

Energy
- No new oil and gas; end fossil subsidies; a rising carbon tax; wind supplying ~70% of electricity by 2030; unleash solar and onshore wind; community ownership; grid/storage upgrades.
- Stop new nuclear and phase out existing reactors.

Fairer economy and tax
- Average £40bn a year green investment in energy, homes, transport, industry, nature and water; bring rail, water and the Big 5 retail energy firms into public ownership.
- Wealth tax on assets over £10m; align capital gains and investment income with earnings; remove NI upper limit; reform inheritance tax; clamp down on avoidance.
- Support SMEs via regional mutual banks and grants; shift to a circular, repair‑and‑reuse economy.

Work and incomes
- Repeal anti‑union laws; a Charter of Workers’ Rights; £15 minimum wage (support for small firms); 10:1 pay ratios; full rights for gig workers; move toward a four‑day week.
- Immediate anti‑poverty measures: +£40/week to Universal Credit; scrap two‑child cap and five‑week wait; uplift disability and carers’ benefits; protect pensions; pathway to Universal Basic Income.

Nature, animals, food
- Rights of Nature; 30% of land and sea protected by 2030; public ownership of water; Clean Air Act; Right to Roam.
- End destructive fishing in MPAs; phase out factory farming, cages and routine antibiotics; ban blood sports; new Animal Protection Commission.
- Triple farm support for agroecology; cut pesticides; boost UK horticulture; free school meals and breakfast clubs.

Education
- Free, inclusive education; scrap tuition fees and restore grants; £8bn for schools and £5bn for SEND; end high‑stakes testing and Ofsted; expand childcare; counsellors and school nurses.

Transport
- Public transport renaissance: nationalise rail; free buses for under‑18s; major bus, rail, cycling and walking investment; halt new road‑building; rapid EV transition with scrappage; 20mph default in built‑up areas; frequent‑flyer levy and no short‑haul flights where rail is viable.

Democracy and rights
- Fair Politics Act: proportional representation, end voter ID, curb big money, elected second chamber, votes at 16; empower local and devolved governments; defend human rights and trans rights; end Prevent and hostile environment; humane asylum with safe routes and right to work.

Global justice and peace
- Back Ukraine, international law and climate justice; immediate ceasefire and recognition of Palestine; end UK arms exports to Israel; restore aid to 1% GNI and increase climate finance; path to rejoin the EU (customs union first); sign the Nuclear Ban Treaty and cancel Trident; reform NATO toward de‑escalation and no‑first‑use.

Judge whether A or B aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "A" | "B"
}
